implemented.change: Cancel superseded CI runs within each pull request or branch ref.
implemented.benefit: Avoid continuing obsolete three-platform Rust checks and dashboard/operational tests.

implemented.change: Cancel superseded main-branch image builds; give every tag and non-main dispatch its own run-specific concurrency group.
implemented.benefit: Avoid obsolete two-platform image builds while retaining every tag release run, including repeated runs for the same tag.

validation.yaml: Both edited workflows parsed successfully with Python PyYAML safe_load.
validation.expressions: Manually inspected: main Docker ref selects stable latest group with cancellation; every other ref selects github.run_id with cancellation false. Unique tag groups prevent GitHub's pending-run replacement behavior.
validation.not_measured: No GitHub workflow was dispatched; elapsed CI savings depend on overlapping pushes.

preserved_safeguards: Full LTO and opt-level 3 prioritize release runtime speed; existing documented compact-profile slowdowns argue against changing the default solely for binary size.
Docker already separates manifest/toolchain/SQLite dependency compilation from source/UI changes, reuses the build stage for both image flavors, and uses native architecture runners.

Asset fingerprints use post-reference-rewrite source content. Changed scripts/dictionaries therefore invalidate their referencing index/i18n assets. Deterministic gzip and unchanged generated declarations remain stable.
Compressed asset cache invalidates its prior fingerprint before replacing the gzip file, preserving recovery after interruption and source reversion.
Asset serving reuses static gzip bytes and one lazy shared identity copy. Conditional 304 responses occur before decompression and use representation-specific validators.
Client authentication precedes request-body decoding. Encoded and decoded sizes remain independently bounded; multi-member/frame decoding preserves trailing-corruption checks.
Admission permits retain request and decoded-byte accounting through response-stream completion or cancellation; defaults bypass accounting overhead when limits are disabled.

remaining_opportunities.finding: Compressed request decoding uses ReaderStream's default chunk capacity; enabled byte admission takes a mutex once per decoded chunk.
remaining_opportunities.recommendation: If large compressed inputs are a measured bottleneck, compare larger decoder output chunks using 1/4/16 MiB gzip and zstd fixtures under concurrency. Retain both size limits, corruption tests and admission cancellation behavior.
remaining_opportunities.status: Unmeasured tuning candidate; no code change.

remaining_opportunities.finding: Fonts have one-year immutable caching under semantic filenames rather than content-versioned URLs. Their existing contract requires filenames to change when bytes change.
remaining_opportunities.recommendation: Preserve filename changes on future font replacement, or extend content versioning to fonts before replacing their contents in place.
remaining_opportunities.status: Existing future asset-update constraint; current fonts unchanged.
